standard_prerequisites: Homotopies: for functions f, g from A to B, an element H of the type product over x of f(x) = g(x), called a homotopy from f to g.
The action of a function on paths: for f from A to B and p in x = y a path in f(x) = f(y), written ap of f applied to p, computing on refl by definition.
Path concatenation with its definitional behaviour on refl.
The induction principle for identity types (path induction) with its conversion rule.
core_obligations: Construct, by path induction on p, for every homotopy H from f to g and every path p in x = y the naturality square identification: H(x) concatenated with ap of g along p equals ap of f along p concatenated with H(y).
Verify that the construction computes correctly on refl x.
proof_roadmap: By path induction, reduce to the case where p is refl x.
In that case the goal becomes H(x) concatenated with refl of g(x) equals refl of f(x) concatenated with H(x), using the definitional computation of ap on reflexivity.
Both sides are equal to H(x) by the unit laws for concatenation with reflexivity, which are definitional; conclude the identification.
difficulty_reason: A single path induction whose reflexivity case is settled by the definitional unit behaviour of concatenation with reflexivity.
